tool_summary: Installs, upgrades, and removes Node.js packages. Runs arbitrary package lifecycle scripts (postinstall, etc.) by default, same risk shape as npm.
platform_notes: yarn behavior and flags are consistent across Linux and macOS. Yarn Classic (v1) and Yarn Berry (v2+) differ in some internals (e.g. Plug'n'Play vs node_modules) but the subcommands and risk shape covered here are the same across both.

rules.description: The --registry flag points yarn at a package registry other than the default. Installing from an untrusted or unfamiliar registry is a common supply-chain attack vector, since yarn runs package lifecycle scripts (postinstall, etc.) by default at install time with the invoking user's privileges.
rules.reversible_note: The package can be removed, but its lifecycle scripts may have already made changes beyond the package's own files.

rules.description: Installing directly from a git URL or a tarball URL bypasses the registry entirely, fetching and executing code from a source that has not gone through any registry review.
rules.reversible_note: The package can be removed, but lifecycle scripts may have already made changes beyond the package's own files.

rules.description: The add subcommand installs a new package; bare install (or yarn with no subcommand) installs all dependencies from the lockfile/package.json. Either runs lifecycle scripts (postinstall, etc.) with the invoking user's privileges at install time.
rules.reversible_note: The package can be removed, but lifecycle scripts may have already made changes beyond the package's own files.

rules.description: The run subcommand (or bare `yarn <script-name>`) executes an arbitrary script defined in package.json's scripts field. The script's content is not inspected by commandant.
rules.reversible_note: Reversibility depends entirely on the script's contents, which commandant does not inspect.
rules.notes: yarn also allows running a package.json script without the explicit `run` keyword (e.g. `yarn build`). This bare-name form is not distinguishable from a yarn subcommand by pattern alone without a list of the project's declared scripts, and is not covered by this rule; it falls through to yarn-package-management.

rules.description: Manages Node.js packages. Read-only subcommands (list, info, why) do not alter system state. Severity here reflects that unrecognized or future yarn subcommands fall through to this rule; known read-only subcommands are not themselves being flagged as risky.
rules.notes: Default bumped to WARNING (not INFO) because this tool's CLI surface evolves quickly; an unmatched/unrecognized subcommand should surface for review rather than silently pass as benign.
